articles.body: Babar Azam reached a significant milestone during Pakistan's fightback against England at Edgbaston on Friday, becoming only the fourth batter to score 2,000 runs as captain in the World Test Championship.The Pakistan batter reached the landmark in the third innings of the third Test against England, joining an exclusive list headed by England's Joe Root, who is also featuring in the match. Ben Stokes and Sri Lanka's Dimuth Karunaratne are the other two batters to have crossed the mark.Babar got there in 41 innings, making him the third-fastest batter to reach 2,000 WTC runs as captain. Root and Karunaratne share the record for reaching the milestone fastest, having done so in 40 innings. articles.title: Who was Madhav Mantri? The Mumbai cricket stalwart with four Tests who helped shape Sunil Gavaskar and stood alongside teenage Sachin Tendulkar in 1990
articles.summary: Cricket News: When the Mumbai Cricket Association decided to name lounges at the Wankhede Stadium after Sachin Tendulkar, Ajinkya Rahane and late Madhav Mantri, the.
articles.body: When the Mumbai Cricket Association decided to name lounges at the Wankhede Stadium after Sachin Tendulkar, Ajinkya Rahane and late Madhav Mantri, the first two names needed little explanation. The third may leave younger cricket fans wondering: who was Madhav Mantri?The answer is a story of influence far greater than his four-Test career suggests.Mantri was a three-time Ranji Trophy-winning captain of Bombay, a national selector and a prominent administrator who played a role in shaping Mumbai cricket's culture. He also had a remarkable connection with two of India's greatest batters, Sunil Gavaskar and Tendulkar, at very different stages of their careers.The man who taught Gavaskar to earn his India capMantri was Gavaskar's maternal uncle, and his influence on the future India great began well before Gavaskar's international debut.As a youngster, Gavaskar was fascinated by an India cap belonging to Mantri. He wanted to have it, but his uncle refused to let him simply inherit it. Gavaskar would have to earn his own.When Gavaskar eventually received an India cap during India's 1971 tour of the West Indies, he did not wear it in the tour matches. He waited until he had actually represented India in a Test.For Mantri, the cap represented something that had to be earned.His own international career was brief. He made his Test debut against England in 1951 and played his last international against Pakistan in 1955. Across four Tests, he scored 67 runs, with a highest score of 39.But those numbers barely tell the story of his standing in Indian domestic cricket.Three Ranji Trophy titles with BombayMantri played 42 Ranji Trophy matches for Bombay and accumulated 2,787 runs at an average of 50.67. His finest innings came against Maharashtra in the 1948-49 season, when he scored 200 in a match that produced 2,376 runs and nine centuries.His greater legacy came as a leader.Mantri captained Bombay to Ranji Trophy titles in 1951-52, 1955-56 and 1956-57, helping establish the foundations of the dominance that would later become synonymous with Mumbai cricket.There was also an unfortunate slice of Test history attached to his career. During the 1952 Headingley Test against England, India were reduced to 0/4 in their second innings, with Fred Trueman and Alec Bedser ripping through the batting order. Mantri was one of those four batters dismissed before India had scored a run.His international career faded. His influence on Mumbai cricket did not.The batting lesson behind Gavaskar's greatnessMantri's impact on Gavaskar went beyond the famous India-cap story.On one occasion, Gavaskar returned home delighted after scoring around 290 in a college match during a huge partnership. But Mantri was less interested in the number. His immediate question was how Gavaskar had been dismissed.Gavaskar explained that he had fallen attempting a lofted shot while his partner remained unbeaten.Mantri's response was straightforward: do not give your wicket away. Make the bowler earn it.That philosophy would become central to Gavaskar's batting. The opener went on to score 10,122 Test runs and became the first batter to cross 10,000 in the format.Mantri's Test tally was only 67.Yet one of the defining principles behind India's first great batting superstar had been reinforced by a man whose own international career lasted just four Tests.From Gavaskar to a teenage TendulkarMantri's influence did not stop with his nephew.He later served as a national selector and played a role in backing Ajit Wadekar's selection for India. He also became president of the Mumbai Cricket Association and treasurer of the BCCI.Then, nearly four decades after his own Test debut, Mantri found himself alongside another teenage Mumbai batting prodigy.He was India's team manager on the 1990 tour of England, when a 17-year-old Tendulkar was beginning to establish himself at international level.At Old Trafford, with India battling to save the second Test, Tendulkar struck an unbeaten 119, his maiden Test century. He became India's youngest Test centurion at the time.Mantri was there as team manager as another Mumbai batter announced himself on the world stage.The teenager's hunger also impressed him. Tendulkar was expected to be rested for a match against Derbyshire but wanted to play because he wanted to face Ian Bishop, one of the fastest bowlers around. He got his chance and scored an unbeaten century.After Tendulkar's Old Trafford hundred, Mantri recalled that the teenager was not simply interested in celebrating. He wanted to know whether he had made mistakes during his innings.For Mantri, who had spent decades emphasising discipline and responsibility, that attitude mattered.Why Madhav Mantri still mattersThat is the real story behind the name now being attached to a lounge at Wankhede.Mantri may have scored only 67 Test runs, but his cricketing footprint was considerably larger. He led Bombay to three Ranji Trophy titles, influenced selection, held senior administrative positions and helped shape the thinking of Gavaskar.Decades later, he was also part of the Indian team setup when Tendulkar scored the first of his 100 international centuries.One Mumbai cricket generation followed another, and Mantri was there in the background for both.The MCA's decision to name a Wankhede lounge after him alongside Tendulkar and Rahane brings that forgotten legacy back into focus.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Heads Dada wins, tails Ponting loses: When Sourav Ganguly pranked Australian captain at toss with 'head-tail' call
articles.summary: Cricket News: Sourav Ganguly is widely regarded as one of the most influential captains in Indian cricket history. During his career, \"Dada\" was known for several m.
articles.body: Sourav Ganguly is widely regarded as one of the most influential captains in Indian cricket history. During his career, "Dada" was known for several memorable moments on and off the field, from making Steve Waugh wait at the toss and celebrating shirtless on the Lord's balcony to clashes with coaches Greg Chappell and John Buchanan, arguments with Shane Warne, and refusing to walk after Graeme Smith claimed a catch.But former Australia captain Michael Clarke has shared another story that shows a lighter side of Ganguly.In his book Eleven Gods and a Billion Indians, author Boria Majumdar quotes Clarke recalling an incident involving Ganguly and Ricky Ponting during a toss in India, although Clarke admits he does not remember which match it was.“One of Clarke’s favourite anecdotes goes thus: Ganguly and Ricky Ponting were out at the toss during one of the matches in India — Clarke doesn’t specifically remember which one — and Ponting had the coin in hand. Just as he flipped the coin, Ganguly, if Clarke is to be believed, said, ‘Head-Tail’.“‘Trust me, mate, that’s what Ricky told me,’ Clarke says, cracking up. ‘Ricky said he couldn’t fathom what had happened with Dada having said Head-Tail. [And, apparently it was said at the speed of lightning.] It had taken Ricky a second or two to come to grips with the situation and by that time the coin had come down. Ganguly just picked it up and said to Ricky, “We’ll bat” and walked off. India had won the toss and were batting. Ricky did not really know what to do or say and all he did was tell us in the dressing room exactly what happened at the toss," Clarke was quoted as saying in the book.Clarke is not sure which match the incident took place in.According to available records, Ganguly won five tosses against Ricky Ponting, and all of those came outside India; twice during the 2003 World Cup and three times in the 2003-04 VB Series. That means Clarke may have mixed up the venue while recalling the story, as Ponting would have been the one calling the toss if the match had been played in India.Clarke, however, clearly states that he does not remember the exact match in which the incident happened.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 1980s AI photo trend: Jasprit Bumrah, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Shreyas Iyer get hilarious makeovers - WATCH
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Social media has found a fun new way to bring the 1980s back, with AI turning modern-day pictures into vintage portraits. The trend has now.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Social media has found a fun new way to bring the 1980s back, with AI turning modern-day pictures into vintage portraits. The trend has now reached the Indian cricket team, with several players enjoying a hilarious surprise ahead of their T20I series against Afghanistan in Delhi.Axar, Abhishek and Bumrah join the funTwo days before the series, the Indian players gathered at their hotel for a photo session. But before it began, they found a table filled with AI-generated pictures of themselves.The portraits, featured in a video shared by the BCCI, showed the players in classic 1980s looks, complete with bell-bottom jeans, big sunglasses and retro hairstyles.India allrounder Axar Patel and Abhishek Sharma picked up the portraits and burst out laughing as they showed them to their teammates. Jasprit Bumrah also joined in the fun.Sanju Samson, Washington Sundar, Shreyas Iyer, Tilak Varma and Shivam Dube checked out their retro pictures and appeared amused by their new 1980s avatars.Ishan Kishan embraces his retro avatarIshan Kishan, who recently led East Zone to Duleep Trophy glory, fully embraced the retro look. He held up his AI-generated picture, sang and posed for the camera as his teammates enjoyed the moment.Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Yash Thakur and Ravi Bishnoi also broke into smiles after seeing their 1980s avatars.India vs Afghanistan T20I seriesIndia and Afghanistan will face each other in a three-match T20I series, starting Sunday at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in Delhi.The second and third T20Is will be played on Tuesday and Thursday at the same venue.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: England vs Pakistan, 3rd Test highlights: England crush Pakistan by 8 wickets to complete 3-0 clean sweep
articles.body: England vs Pakistan, 3rd Test Live Score: Pakistan fight back after early blows Pakistan were bowled out for 449 on day three of the final Test on Friday, leaving England a target of 130 to win and complete a 3-0 series sweep. The tourists, looking to avoid a clean sweep, produced a strong response after England made 453 in their first innings. Razaullah provided the late fireworks with a brilliant 81 on his Test debut at No. 9. Earlier, Shan Masood and Babar Azam led Pakistan's fightback after the visitors suffered a disastrous start. Masood made a defiant 95, falling just five runs short of what would have been his first century of the tour. He and Azan Awais came together in the first over with Pakistan 0-2 down and rebuilt the innings with a 125-run partnership. It was Pakistan's first century partnership of the series. .England vs Pakistan, 3rd Test Live Score: Hello and welcome! articles.title: India vs Afghanistan 1st T20I: Delhi Traffic Police issue advisory amid BRICS Summit
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: The Delhi Traffic Police on Saturday issued a traffic advisory ahead of the India-Afghanistan T20I at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in New Delhi.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Delhi Traffic Police on Saturday issued a traffic advisory ahead of the India-Afghanistan T20I at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in New Delhi on September 13.Traffic restrictions, diversions and parking rules will be in place in and around the stadium from 1400 hours onwards.The advisory comes at a time when New Delhi is also hosting the ongoing BRICS Summit.In a post on X, Delhi Traffic Police said, "In connection with the India–Afghanistan T20 Cricket Match at Arun Jaitley Stadium on 13.09.2026, traffic restrictions, diversions and parking regulations will be in place in and around the stadium area from 1400 hrs onwards."The traffic police asked commuters to plan their journeys in advance and avoid unnecessary travel through the stadium area."Commuters are advised to plan their journeys in advance, avoid unnecessary travel through the match venue area, use alternate routes wherever feasible and follow the directions of traffic personnel," the advisory said."Spectators are requested to use only designated entry, parking and app-based taxi pick-up/drop-off points. For real-time traffic updates, follow the official social media handles of Delhi Traffic Police," it said."Motorists are requested to remain patient, follow traffic rules, and cooperate with traffic personnel deployed in the area. Please follow diversion signs and traffic directions to avoid congestion," Delhi Traffic Police said.The police also advised commuters to follow the instructions of traffic personnel deployed in the area and use alternate routes wherever possible.The first T20I between India and Afghanistan will be played at the Arun Jaitley Stadium on September 13.With traffic restrictions beginning from 1400 hours, commuters and spectators have been advised to plan their travel accordingly.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
